PullRequest.Title: sessions: Add chat tab presentation menu
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- expose `sessions.showChatTabs` in the session header overflow menu
- offer checked **Multiple** and **Single** presentation choices between the New Chat and Pin/Close groups
- update accessibility guidance and add regression coverage for the menu and configuration updates

Follow-up to #336595.

## Testing

- `npm run compile-client`
- `npm run hygiene`
- ESLint on changed files
- 40 focused session action and accessibility help tests

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench/session view startup and construction of session header or chat-tab toolbars
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Module evaluation registers one new MenuId, one submenu descriptor, and two action descriptors; each rendered SessionBarToolbar then evaluates the additional local context-key-gated submenu item. No asynchronous work or external operation must complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of currently constructed session/header and chat-group toolbars; the diff adds constant-size menu metadata and one context expression per toolbar, not work proportional to session history or chat contents.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous menu registration and local context-key evaluation; no queue, limiter, IPC, subprocess, filesystem, database, or network concurrency is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Menu descriptors are stored once in MenuRegistry. Toolbar evaluation uses in-memory registry and context-key state; there is no cold-cache fetch, retry, or negative-cache path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete production diff and all SessionBarToolbar construction sites show only static menu/action registration and in-memory context conditions on this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact simultaneous toolbar count varies with split chat groups, but the incremental work remains constant per rendered toolbar and allocates no heavyweight UI or retained per-session collection.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added eager work is a few static descriptors and one constant-time menu condition per toolbar, with no expensive boundary or scaling allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening the session overflow menu and its Show Chat Tabs submenu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The active toolbar resolves the submenu and two checked actions from MenuRegistry and evaluates config.sessions.showChatTabs from context-key state before displaying the menu. All work is local and synchronous.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly two presentation actions for one opened menu, independent of the number of sessions and chats after the context condition selects eligible sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI interaction on the UI thread; no parallel work, serialization queue, or external call occurs merely from opening the menu.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The registered submenu/actions are reused; checked state reads the already-maintained configuration context key. There is no cache miss or recomputation over session data.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed action descriptors contain only titles, ordering, context expressions, and menu IDs until an action is invoked.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Menu framework implementation details can add normal action-object creation, but the diff contributes only two fixed actions and does not change menu cardinality with user data.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: menu-open cost is bounded and contains no changed expensive boundary, fan-out, or retained growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: Selecting Multiple or Single chat presentation from the session overflow menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command awaits IConfigurationService.updateValue. If the selected value differs, configuration persistence writes and reloads the relevant settings model; the configuration event then toggles tab/header visibility for currently rendered groups and rerenders the active title. Selecting the already-effective value makes deriveConfigurationTargets return no targets, so no write occurs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/sessionsActions.ts:1712 and :1731, transitively src/vs/sessions/services/configuration/browser/configurationService.ts:161-213 or the workbench configuration service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the sessions.showChatTabs value to the selected profile/workspace settings resource through ConfigurationEditing, then reload configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero writes for a warm no-op selection; otherwise one target and one settings write/reload for this non-undefined value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The setting and identical persistence/UI-reaction path already existed through Settings, but the base revision had no session-overflow command that invoked it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action promise waits for persistence/reload before completion; reactive UI consumers update from the resulting configuration change.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit user selection; subsequent UI visibility work scales with the small number of currently rendered chat groups, not all saved sessions or historical chats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One awaited update per invocation. ConfigurationEditing serializes writes through its existing shared queue; this diff creates no per-chat calls or aggregate concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current configuration is inspected in memory. Equal values are coalesced into zero targets and no write; changed values use the existing authoritative configuration reload rather than a new cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both new run methods each issue one updateValue; target derivation short-circuits equal values and chooses one target for a non-undefined value, while UI consumers only toggle existing presentation observables.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Settings write latency depends on the profile/file-service backend and rendered split-group count, but frequency is explicitly user-driven and cardinality is bounded to one write per actual change.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the sole external operation is the expected, bounded persistence for an explicit presentation change, with no fan-out, burst, or repeated work introduced.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The provider composes its existing fixed list of localized guidance and performs the existing in-memory configuration read; the diff only lengthens one selected guidance string.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant number of help strings per explicit help invocation; the added text does not scale with sessions, chats, transcript size, or history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous content construction with no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work introduced by the changed strings.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Localization strings are static and the configuration value is read from the already-loaded configuration model; no new cache lifecycle exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines only replace localized string literals, and provider registration/invocation and configuration access are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact final rendered text length varies by localization, but the increment is fixed and small relative to the already large constant help content.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: fixed-size text growth does not establish meaningful CPU, memory, rendering, or boundary cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and traced startup/menu construction, menu opening, action-driven configuration persistence, reactive presentation updates, and accessibility-help generation. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression was found.
